nphi.title: CDC Caribbean and Central America Regional Office (CCAMRO)
nphi.with: Caribbean Public Health Agency (CARPHA) and its Reference Laboratory; Council of Ministers of Health of Central America (COMISCA); Gorgas Memorial Institute; SENACYT; INDICASAT
nphi.summary: Launched in 2024 in Panama City, CDC's CCAMRO covers 21 countries, working with CARPHA, COMISCA and Panama's Gorgas Memorial Institute on early warning, surveillance, laboratory strengthening and emergency response capacity.

nphi.title: Pandemic Fund Caribbean project: integrated early warning, surveillance and laboratory systems
nphi.with: Inter-American Development Bank (implementing entity); also Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, St Kitts and Nevis, St Lucia, St Vincent and the Grenadines
nphi.summary: US$16 million Pandemic Fund grant led regionally by CARPHA for 12 member states, covering regional coordination, surveillance, laboratory systems, workforce development and emergency management.

nphi.title: CDC Haiti country office
nphi.with: Ministry of Public Health and Population (MSPP); National Public Health Laboratory (LNSP); Haiti FETP
nphi.summary: CDC's Haiti office (2002) works with MSPP and the National Public Health Laboratory on surveillance, lab capacity, emergency response and the FETP (since 2011), plus HIV/TB, cholera/WASH, NTDs and malaria.

nphi.title: C19-HaitiLab – COVID-19 diagnosis and surveillance support to Haiti's LNSP
nphi.with: Laboratoire National de Santé Publique (LNSP); GHESKIO; Agence Française de Développement (AFD)
nphi.summary: AFD-funded project (2021–2024) with Haiti's national public health laboratory and GHESKIO to strengthen COVID-19 diagnosis and surveillance.

nphi.title: CCASAnet – Caribbean, Central and South America network for HIV epidemiology
nphi.with: Clinical and research sites in seven countries
nphi.summary: NIAID-funded regional HIV epidemiology network coordinated by Vanderbilt with clinical research sites in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Haiti, Honduras, Mexico and Peru.

nphi.title: Argentina–PAHO–CARICOM triangular project on AMR detection and surveillance
nphi.actor: ANLIS Dr. Carlos G. Malbrán – INEI
nphi.with: CARICOM Secretariat; PAHO/WHO; SENASA; Argentine Fund for International Cooperation (FO.AR); Best-dos Santos Public Health Laboratory (Barbados) and other CARICOM national laboratories
nphi.summary: Two-year FO.AR-funded triangular cooperation (2019–2021) in which Malbrán's INEI hosted internships and trained Caribbean laboratory technologists to strengthen clinical AMR diagnosis and surveillance in 14 CARICOM countries.

nphi.title: SPHaïtiLab – strengthening Haiti's national public health laboratory and laboratory policy
nphi.with: Laboratoire National de Santé Publique (LNSP) Haiti; Direction d'Épidémiologie, de Laboratoire et de Recherche (DELR); GHESKIO; Institut Africain de Santé Publique (Burkina Faso)
nphi.type: Project (EU Supporting Public Health Institutes programme)
nphi.summary: Consortium project supporting Haiti's health ministry in developing a national laboratory policy and strengthening the LNSP's public health functions, including lab assessments, an information system, training and a five-year LNSP…

nphi.title: Rebuilding Haiti's public health infrastructure after the 2010 earthquake
nphi.with: Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population (MSPP); DELR at the Laboratoire National de Santé Publique complex
nphi.summary: CDC Foundation partnership raising over US$3.2 million to build a new MSPP central office and a DELR building at the national public health laboratory complex, housing Haitian surveillance, epidemiology and laboratory staff alongside CDC…

nphi.title: Brazil–Cuba–Haiti tripartite cooperation to rebuild Haiti's health system
nphi.with: Cuban Ministry of Public Health (medical brigades); Haitian Ministry of Public Health and Population
nphi.summary: Tripartite agreement signed in March 2010 after the earthquake: Brazil financed (R$135 million) facilities, equipment, an epidemiological surveillance centre, vaccination and training, while Cuba provided doctors and technicians.
